notation.meaning: Area between the line of equality and the Lorenz curve

blocks.md: The Gini coefficient turns a Lorenz curve into a single number between zero and one. Zero means everyone has the same income; one means a single person has everything. Geometrically it is the size of the gap between the Lorenz curve and the line of perfect equality. Another way to read it: pick two people at random, and the Gini is half their typical income gap relative to the average income.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: It is the most widely reported inequality statistic, so knowing what it does and does not capture is essential for comparing countries and years.
The most common single-number summary of the [Lorenz Curve](note:lorenz-curve).
$A$ is the area between the 45° line of equality and the Lorenz curve; $B$ is the area under the Lorenz curve. Since $A + B = \tfrac12$, equivalently $G = 1 - 2B$.
If all $z_i \geq 0$, $G \in [0,1]$: 0 is complete equality, 1 is one person holding everything. Often reported ×100 (e.g. 45.0).

blocks.prompt: The gap between the 45° line and the Lorenz curve is $A$, and $G = A/(A+B) = 1 - 2B$. Raise the spread of log wages and watch the gap and $G$ grow together.

predict.ask: Raise the spread and the Lorenz curve sags further below the 45° line. In $G = A/(A+B)$, which areas change?
options: A grows and B shrinks by the same amount, because A + B = 1/2 always
A grows and B stays the same
Both grow, because the spread of incomes grows
predict.why: $A + B$ is the triangle under the line of equality, $1/2$ for every distribution. As the curve sags, area moves from $B$ to $A$, so $G = A/(A+B) = 2A = 1 - 2B$ rises: from 0.28 at a log-wage spread of 0.5 to 0.52 at a spread of 1.
feedback: $A$ and $B$ together fill the triangle under the line of equality, so they always add to $1/2$. Whatever $A$ gains, $B$ loses.
The Lorenz curve uses income *shares*, so its square has area 1 and the triangle under the 45° line is $1/2$ whatever the incomes are. $A + B$ cannot grow.

blocks.md: Equivalent **mean absolute difference** form — the most intuitive:
The Gini is half the average absolute gap between two randomly drawn people, relative to the mean.
**Worked example**: for the nine incomes in [Lorenz Curve](note:lorenz-curve), both formulas give $G = 0.167$.

| Property | Gini |
| --- | --- |
| Scale invariant | Yes |
| Transfer principle (rich → poor transfer lowers it) | Yes |
| Most sensitive to | The **middle** of the distribution |
| Subgroup decomposable | **No** — only with non-overlapping groups |
